body.en: The expedition was part of the *Students on Ice* programme, led by the Canadian Geoff Green. It takes high-school students to the ends of the world to give them an understanding of, and respect for, the planet. Green believes young people are at an age when they absorb, learn and, most importantly, act, unlike older leaders who are busy with other things.

Ecology: everything depends on the food chain.
Earth's history: from Gondwana to today.

body.en: The account explores climate change and global warming, the fragile balance of ecosystems, and the long history of the earth compared with the short history of humans. It urges responsibility and hope: if the next generation sees the effects for itself, it can lead the change. Its tone is reflective, informative and gently persuasive.

problem.en: Why does Geoff Green take students rather than policymakers to Antarctica?

steps.en: Students are at an age to absorb and learn.
Seeing the effects first-hand leaves a lasting impression.
They will be the policymakers of the future.
So they are most likely to act.

answer.en: Geoff Green believes that young people absorb ideas, learn quickly and, above all, act. Seeing glaciers retreating and ice shelves collapsing first-hand leaves a deep impression. As future leaders and citizens, they can carry this understanding into decisions, which makes them the best hope for protecting the planet.
